item.title: Over one thousand Grade 12 students sit for National Exams in MBP
item.description: A total of 1, 069 grade twelve students are sitting for their National Examinations this week across seven secondary schools in Milne Bay province. ‎Education authorities say the distribution of examination papers and deployment of examination invigilators to respective schools were executed smoothly ahead of the examinations this week.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 1, 069 grade twelve students are sitting for their National Examinations this week across seven secondary schools in Milne Bay province.

‎Education authorities say the distribution of examination papers and deployment of examination invigilators to respective schools were executed smoothly ahead of the examinations this week.

‎Milne Bay Provincial Education Principal Advisor, Roma Tuidam says the divisions priority this week is to ensure the safe delivery of examination papers and the timely arrival of invigilators at examination rooms.

‎‎"Our priority at this point in time is to ensure that the security of the exam papers are being moved from this office to our respective schools and ensuring that exam room protocols are observed at all times.” Tuidam said.

‎‎Meanwhile, 2, 517 grade 10 students from across thirteen schools in the province sat for their national examination last week, while 4, 525 grade eight students are expected to sit for their national Examinations next week from October 19- 22.

‎Tuidam said most grade 10 examination papers have already been returned to the Education Division in Alotau, with papers from remote schools yet to arrive this week alongside their respective invigilators. The Gr. 10 examination papers are scheduled to be marked next week in Alotau.

item.title: Middle Fly first in southern region to submit 2025 DSIP report
item.description: Middle Fly District in Western Province has set a benchmark for accountability and compliance, becoming the 8th district nationally and the 1st in the Southern Region to submit its 2025 District Services Improvement Program Reports through the Digital Bilum Platform. District Administrator and Chief Executive Officer of the Middle Fly District Development Authority, Petrus Malongim, formally submi
item.content:encoded:
Middle Fly District in Western Province has set a benchmark for accountability and compliance, becoming the 8th district nationally and the 1st in the Southern Region to submit its 2025 District Services Improvement Program Reports through the Digital Bilum Platform.

District Administrator and Chief Executive Officer of the Middle Fly District Development Authority, Petrus Malongim, formally submitted the district's acquittals to the Secretary for the Department of Implementation and Rural Development, Aihi Vaki, via the Bilum Online Platform in Port Moresby on Monday

Malongim said the achievement reflects the commitment of his small team to embrace digital transformation for transparency and accountability.

"Our new district status, skeleton capacity and limited facilities are not limitations, but motivation for us to press on and ensure we comply with national reporting requirements," Malongim said.

Middle Fly Open MP, Maso Hewabi, who was present to support the submission, said he is proud of his district's achievement.

"Being the first District from Southern Region and eight in the country despite being very remote and a new district, we are proud to join other districts to rise to that level. Us being new and remote should not be an excuse when it comes to being accountable as stewards of the people of Middle Fly. Their money must be accounted holistically," MP Hewabi said.

Hewabi said the main challenge was logistics and inaccessibility in collecting reports, but his team overcame it by creating a Contractors WhatsApp Group where contractors provide weekly progressive updates.

"With this, our reporting and acquittal is very, very simple," he said.

He said the compliance will now allow the DDA to track past spending and plan future projects better in terms of sectors and locations.

MP Hewabi commended his administration staff for working in unity despite operating on a skeleton structure.

"I have a great team not because of quantity but their strength is unity and respect for each other. I thank DA Mr Petrus Malongim, DFM Mr Kewo Kapala and electoral staff for working together," he said.

He urged other districts to embrace the platform, saying it is user-friendly.

"I urge every district to comply. We all have our own challenges, but this should not be an excuse. It's 51 years of our country. Let's migrate into this new digital platform," Hewabi said.

Hewabi added that his next priorities are to establish an Electronic Transfer System for the District Treasury, build district administration infrastructure to boost staffing, and improve communication services across Lake Murray, Nomad, Strickland-Bosavi and surrounding areas.

The Bilum Platform is an online system used by DIRD to receive and manage acquittals for funds allocated to provinces and districts across the country.

item.title: GPHA nurses undergo emergency and critical care training
item.description: A two-week Emergency and Critical Care System Strengthening Initiative training is currently underway for nurses of the Gulf Provincial Health Authority (GPHA) in Kerema. The training comes under the Regional Emergency and Critical Care Systems Strengthening Initiative, an organization sponsored by the Australian Government in partnership with the National Department of Health (NDoH) and St John A
item.content:encoded:
A two-week Emergency and Critical Care System Strengthening Initiative training is currently underway for nurses of the Gulf Provincial Health Authority (GPHA) in Kerema.

The training comes under the Regional Emergency and Critical Care Systems Strengthening Initiative, an organization sponsored by the Australian Government in partnership with the National Department of Health (NDoH) and St John Ambulance Services PNG.

The training counterfunded by the Gulf Provincial Health Authority through the office of the Curative Health Services, aims to upskill frontline nurses to better respond to emergency cases encountered daily.

A total of 18 participants are attending, comprising of four specialists from the emergency unit and nurses from other units of the Kerema General Hospital. To ensure health services continue uninterrupted, participants have been divided into two groups, with both groups to undergo the same training a week apart.

Manager Nursing Services Sr. Helen Morito said the on-site training is cost-effective and allows more staff to attend. She highlighted that in most cases; it is the nurses on the ground who deal with emergency cases in the absence of doctors and physicians.

"Trainings like this help nurses reflect on how we treat patients — whether it was the right way or not. Most of the times we tend to forget what we were taught, and this will help refresh their minds. Most times it is the nurses who are on the ground attending to emergencies when there are no doctors," Sr. Morito said.

Hospital Manager Jim Lapai echoed similar sentiments, noting that it is often nurses who are first to attend to emergencies.

"Most times it is the nurses on the ground that deal with the emergency cases. I hope that with this training they can do their best in delivering their service to our patients. The level of work done has not reached the standard level. Most work done is 50/50 and not 100% like it should be."

He added that this is the first time a team has come to do this training and help staff upskill their knowledge when dealing with emergency cases

Provincial Health Training Coordinator Noah Mavoho, who has been vocal about continuous training, welcomed the initiative, especially with the developments happening at Kerema General Hospital.

"All staff should be equipped and ready to work and meet some of the requirements of the new level 5 hospital that is currently in progress of being built," Mavoho said.

Facilitating the training is Dr. Ovia Bue, an Emergency Physician from the Central Provincial Health Authority. alongside Sr. Eresi Iowa an Emergency nurse from the Port Moresby General Hospital. Dr. Bue said the training will focus on basic emergency care and the Interagency Integrated Triage Tool (IITT).

"The first week will be training, and the second week will be the implementation of the IITT system in the hospital," Dr. Bue explained.

The group-based approach ensures that while one group is in training, the other remains on duty, keeping essential services running at the GPHA.

Once fully implemented, the IITT triage system is expected to significantly improve emergency response and patient outcomes in Gulf Province.

item.title: Cancer needs comprehensive approach
item.description: Director of Medical Services at Port Moresby General Hospital, Dr Kone Sobi, says cancer treatment in Papua New Guinea needs a comprehensive approach, covering both hospital care and public health awareness. Dr Sobi told NBC News this must include prevention and screening strategies to improve patient outcomes.
item.content:encoded:
Director of Medical Services at Port Moresby General Hospital, Dr Kone Sobi, says cancer treatment in Papua New Guinea needs a comprehensive approach, covering both hospital care and public health awareness.

Dr Sobi told NBC News this must include prevention and screening strategies to improve patient outcomes.

He said most patients present to hospital at quite advanced stages of cancer due to lack of awareness or information.

"Maybe they don't know that it's a cancer, evolving cancer disease process. So by the time they come to the hospital and diagnosis are made, say for instance, breast cancer, cervical cancer, mouth cancer, these diseases are quite advanced stages. And some of them can be very subtle," Dr Sobi said.

He believes having robust screening services within communities would help patients know the status of their cancer at an early stage.

Dr Sobi said early detection of common cancers like cervical cancer will ensure better outcomes with treatment.

He added that common cancers in the country include oral and mouth cancers, which are quite common, followed by breast cancer in women.

In children, he said common cancers include leukemia, a bloodstream cancer.

Dr Sobi said while some cancers are very challenging to treat, early diagnosis and treatment will see better outcomes for patients.

item.title: Enga finally gets its own jail
item.description: Enga Province now has its own correctional facility, a public service the province has long lacked. The Mukurumanda Correctional Facility was officially opened on Monday, October 12, by Prime Minister James Marape, who is also the Minister for Correctional Services.
item.content:encoded:
Enga Province now has its own correctional facility, a public service the province has long lacked.

The Mukurumanda Correctional Facility was officially opened on Monday, October 12, by Prime Minister James Marape, who is also the Minister for Correctional Services.

The opening means offenders from Enga can now be held within their home province, allowing family members to visit them without travelling to Western Highlands Province. It will also ease the burden on Baisu Correctional Institution, which previously accommodated prisoners from Enga.

The opening ceremony began with a parade by Correctional Service officers, followed by a guard of honour for Correctional Service Commissioner Noel Sarei, Prime Minister James Marape and Enga Governor Sir Peter Ipatas.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sir Peter said that when he became governor of Enga, he was determined to complete the legacy of the province's founding leaders by ensuring that important institutions they had initiated were completed and operational.

He said the Mukurumanda Correctional Facility was one such legacy project, originally envisioned by the late Sir Pato Kakaraya in 1987, with construction beginning in 1998.

“For thirty years, I've been carrying papers of projects and walking from one office to another in Waigani, not through any subordinate but by myself to develop Enga Province, and the Mukurumanda CIS facility is one of them,” Sir Peter said.

He said the responsibility for establishing national institutions should rest with the National Government and the relevant government agencies.

“It is not the provincial government's job but the Correctional Service and the National Government's job to look into provinces and take ownership of national functions and national institutions,” Sir Peter said.

In response to the governor's remarks, Prime Minister James Marape acknowledged that the Government had failed the people of Enga by allowing the project to remain incomplete for so many years.

Mr Marape also spoke about further funding to be considered towards completing the Mukurumanda Correctional Facility.

He also said outstanding landowner payments would be looked into to help ensure the facility could operate fully without disruption.

The opening of the Mukurumanda Correctional Facility followed the combined efforts of Correctional Services, the National Government and the Enga Provincial Government.

Following the official opening, Mr Marape toured the facility and visited the inmates.

The facility is already housing prisoners from Enga who were previously held at Baisu Correctional Institution in Western Highlands Province.

Addressing the inmates, Mr Marape encouraged them to abide by the law and work towards rehabilitation so they could return to society.

Also present at the opening were Police Minister Sir John Pundari and Wapenamanda MP Miki Kaeok.

item.title: Electoral Commission faces staffing shortages ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: The Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections has heard that many Papua New Guinea Electoral Commission staff have reached the compulsory retirement age or are on short-term contracts. Electoral Commissioner Dr Nicole Haley revealed this at the committee’s public hearing in Port Moresby recently.
item.content:encoded:
The Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections has heard that many Papua New Guinea Electoral Commission staff have reached the compulsory retirement age or are on short-term contracts.

Electoral Commissioner Dr Nicole Haley revealed this at the committee’s public hearing in Port Moresby recently.

Appearing before the committee for the first time, Dr Haley provided an update on preparations for the 2027 elections.

She said staffing was a major concern and a longstanding challenge for the Commission.

According to Dr Haley, the Commission has 105 established positions, of which 33 are vacant, while 12 staff have exceeded the compulsory retirement age.

“A lot of our election manager positions, they're certainly the most senior positions in the provinces, so you know, let's probably say that they're in leadership roles,” Dr Haley said.

The Commission also employs 99 casual staff, some of whom have worked for more than 10 years.

Dr Haley said the Commission was considering succession planning by moving experienced staff into vacant positions and seconding personnel from other government agencies.

“They call them semi-permanent; these are casual staff that some of whom have been employed in the Electoral Commission for 10 and 15 years.

“They've just been on continual contracts because the Electoral Commission hasn't done a proper establishment review during that time. It clearly needs more positions than it has,” Dr Haley said.

Going forward, the Electoral Commission is working with the Department of Personnel Management to review its organisational structure in preparation for the 2027 elections, which is now about six months away.

item.title: Police crackdown on illegal PMV protest in POM
item.description: Twenty PMV buses were impounded today and their drivers and crews arrested after staging an illegal protest over rising fuel prices, disrupting the city’s public transport system. Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD-Central Commander Benjamin Turi personally led the operation, warning that police will arrest any PMV operators who overcharge passengers or engage in unlawful demonstrations.
item.content:encoded:
Twenty PMV buses were impounded today and their drivers and crews arrested after staging an illegal protest over rising fuel prices, disrupting the city’s public transport system.

Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD-Central Commander Benjamin Turi personally led the operation, warning that police will arrest any PMV operators who overcharge passengers or engage in unlawful demonstrations.

“This is a warning to all PMV operators. We have impounded 20 buses and arrested their drivers and crews. If you overcharge passengers or stop work to stage illegal protests, you will be arrested. If you want to stop work, take your bus home instead of forcing others to join your protest,” ACP Turi said.

He stressed that fuel price decisions are made by the government and that operators must use proper channels to raise concerns rather than holding the city “at ransom.”

Turi highlighted the impact on school children, especially Grade 12 students currently sitting exams, who rely on PMVs as their only mode of transport.

The Commander also condemned the practice of buses failing to complete routes while charging multiple fares.

“We have buses charging K2 from Gerehu to Waigani, then another K2 to 4 Mile, and again K2 to town. That’s a rip-off unless you complete your route,” he said.

Police will now monitor bus stops to ensure compliance with fare regulations.

Turi reiterated that operators must abide by rules set by the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (ICCC) and follow lawful avenues to express grievances.

item.title: Drought dries up Arokoi river in Kutubu

item.content:encoded:
More than a thousand people who depend on the main Arokoi river in the Kutubu area of Southern Highlands province are now looking for water for consumption following El Nino induced drought that dried up the river system.

The affected communities are Kaipu 1, Kaipu 2 and Sisibia 1, Sisibia 2 including nearby villages that depend on the main Arokoi river that provides for drinking, cooking and daily use by the people.

The villages also host the Kutubu Petroleum Development License 2 (PDL 2) PNG Liquified Natural Gas project.

Community Leaders Kenny Sasue, Justin Atakaro, Alexs Asi Ware, Freddy Daniel Boko and Gibson Sasue has expressed concerns, appealing to authorities about the impacts of the El Nino induced drought that is affecting their communities.

Kenny Sasue said Arokoi river is the main river that people rely on and also the PNG LNG project developers Santos and ExxonMobil use for the project facilities in the area and the prolong drought has really affected the river system.

“This is a big river that our people including mothers and children use for drinking, cooking and daily use for washing but with the dry season, it has dried up to a stream that it might dry up altogether in the next two weeks or after one month,” Sasue said.

“The small streams that we use to wash and filter our sago have all dried up and we don’t know where we will get the water for consumption after one month if the main Arokoi river dry up altogether”.

“We appeal to PNG LNG project developers Santos and ExxonMobil and to the government especially Prime Minister James Marape to hear our plight,” Kenny Sasue said.

“We also appeal to our local MP for Nipa Kutubu Dr. Billy Joseph for assistance as some of our people have died due to the impacts of the dry season” he said.

The community in the Kutubu area are among others nationwide facing the impact of El Nino induced drought.

The National Weather Service has warned that the El Nino peak is expected during the month of October to December and into next year (2027).
